cards.explanation: The answer is water. The verse says it plainly: “They camped at Rephidim, but there was no water for the people to drink.” (Exodus 17:1) A whole congregation of people, and nothing for them to drink. That's a one star review and a very short sentence.

The answer is the LORD. Moses asks the people, “Why do you test the LORD?” (Exodus 17:2) They had been contending with Moses, and his question brings the LORD into it. I bet he said it with one eyebrow up, too.

The answer is True. The thirsty people grumble, “Why have you brought us out of Egypt…to make us and our children and livestock die of thirst?” (Exodus 17:3) Notice they bring in the kids and the livestock too. Everybody in camp is part of that complaint.

The answer is that Moses cried out to the LORD. (Exodus 17:4) The whole camp is in his face, and he takes it straight to God. I think that's the right move every time, friends. When the crowd gets loud, go to the One who is already listening.

The answer is the staff he struck the Nile with, friends. The LORD says, “Take along in your hand the staff with which you struck the Nile, and go.” (Exodus 17:5) Moses already knows this staff, so he doesn't have to go shopping for a new one. Then the LORD says He will stand there before him by the rock at Horeb. (Exodus 17:6) I once kept my own tools close at hand too, because you never know which one the day is going to call for.

The answer is strikes, friends! The LORD says, “And when you strike the rock, water will come out of it for the people to drink.” (Exodus 17:6) A rock. In a desert. And water is coming out of it. I've pressed a lot of dough in my day, and not once has a rock given me a drink. The LORD also says He will stand there before Moses by the rock, so Moses isn't doing this alone.

The answer is False. Moses struck the rock “…in the sight of the elders of Israel.” (Exodus 17:6) The LORD had told him to take some of the elders along, so they were right there watching. It was a front-row seat to water coming out of a rock.

The answer is quarreled. The verse says Moses named the place Massah and Meribah “…because the Israelites quarreled, and because they tested the LORD…” (Exodus 17:7) The text gives two reasons, and quarreling is the first. Some places get named for the view. This one got named for what the people did.

The answer is Joshua, friends! Moses tells him, “Choose some of our men and go out to fight the Amalekites.” (Exodus 17:9) Then the very next verse says Joshua did as Moses had instructed him. (Exodus 17:10) The text gives us the order and then the doing. I wish my mornings were that tidy when I face a full batch of dough.

The answer is hilltop. Moses says, “Tomorrow I will stand on the hilltop with the staff of God in my hand.” (Exodus 17:9) Joshua is the one told to go out and fight, and Moses takes the hilltop. That hilltop ends up mattering a lot.

The answer is that Moses holds up his hands. The text says, “As long as Moses held up his hands, Israel prevailed…” (Exodus 17:11) It's an odd thing to hang a battle on, if you ask me. But that's what the verse says.

The answer is that Aaron and Hur set a stone under Moses and hold his hands up, friends. They “…took a stone and put it under him, and he sat on it.” Then Aaron and Hur held his hands up, “…one on each side…” (Exodus 17:12) Moses gets a seat and two helpers. I could have used a Hur or two in my drawer days.

The answers are side and sun. Aaron and Hur held his hands up, “…one on each side…” (Exodus 17:12) One helper per arm, and both hands stay up. Nobody has to pick a favorite arm. Their help kept his hands steady “…until the sun went down.” (Exodus 17:12) That's the end point the verse gives. His hands had grown heavy, so I'm glad he had company, friends.

The answer is reminder. The LORD says, “Write this on a scroll as a reminder and recite it to Joshua…” (Exodus 17:14) So the command is to write it down and say it out loud. Good habit, friends. I keep my recipes written down too.

The answer is that the LORD will utterly blot out their memory. He says, “…I will utterly blot out the memory of Amalek from under heaven.” (Exodus 17:14) The reason for the scroll comes right in the same breath. It's a serious word from the LORD, so I'll just say it plainly and leave it there.

The answer is The LORD Is My Banner. Moses built an altar and named it that. (Exodus 17:15) Then he said, “The LORD will war against Amalek from generation to generation.” (Exodus 17:16) The name points straight to the LORD.

The answer is False. Moses says, “The LORD will war against Amalek from generation to generation.” (Exodus 17:16) So it isn't one generation, it reaches down through many. I think the LORD wanted it remembered.
